rule: mixed: the rule is fireable and records that hunted nightmoths flee toward lights, but 'dimmer' is dropped entirely — a comparative used as a bare modifier with no stated comparand has no encoding, so the parse says only that they flee to lights and the whole point of the rule is lost. Supply the standard: 'Hunted nightmoths flee to lights that are dimmer than the lights they leave.'
texts: bad: two losses at once — 'dimmer' is dropped again (the destination is just 'lantern'), and 'the surviving nightmoths' becomes a free-floating condition, so the rule reads 'if any sky-cat hunts anywhere and any nightmoth is surviving, that moth flees', with no tie between the hunt and which moths survived it, and it waits on a standing 'is surviving' fact nothing will ever assert. Make the surviving a finite clause tied to the hunt and give the comparative a standard: 'When sky-cats hunt at a lantern-row, the nightmoths that survive the hunt flee to a lantern dimmer than that lantern-row.'

mixed: the rule fires and the move to the Hollows is right, but 'surviving' lands in the conclusion as a property of the moth group as a whole, so the rule derives a new group that is 'surviving' rather than restricting which moths move — and a member-level description predicated of a group symbol is exactly what the instruction set bars. Turn the modifier into a finite relative clause: 'If sky-cats hunt at a lantern-row, the nightmoths that survive the hunt move to the Hollows.'

bad: this rule is dead — the fireability check flags it, because the participial 'fleeing nightmoths' forces both the fleeing and the reaching into premise terms nothing can ever match, so no arrival at the Hollows will ever trigger the threads; on top of that 'extra' is predicated of the thread group as a whole, and 'the Hollows lanterns' is turned into a containment claim the sentence never makes. Give each event its own finite verb and state the location with a preposition: 'When nightmoths flee and reach the Hollows, the lanterns at the Hollows gain extra silken threads.'
